question: What happens when retrieval is messy?

update.answer:
The final answer is:

When retrieval is messy, it can lead to retrieval-induced forgetting, where previously learned information is lost due to the reactivation of previously learned material during retrieval (Roediger & Karpicke, 2006). This can result in decreased performance on subsequent memory tests and decreased memory retention (McDaniel & Leitner, 1994).
